# dhgeqz

> Computes the eigenvalues of a real matrix pair (H,T) where H is upper Hessenberg and T is upper triangular, using the QZ method.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dhgeqz from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dhgeqz';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dhgeqz(
    order,
    job, compq, compz,
    N,
    ilo, ihi,
    H, LDH,
    T, LDT,
    ALPHAR, strideALPHAR,
    ALPHAI, strideALPHAI,
    BETA, strideBETA,
    Q, LDQ,
    Z, LDZ,
    WORK
) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `job` | `"eigenvalues" \| "schur"` | Specifies the operation type<br>One of `'eigenvalues'`, `'schur'`. |
| `compq` | `"none" \| "initialize" \| "update"` | Specifies the operation type<br>One of `'initialize'`, `'none'`, `'update'`. |
| `compz` | `"none" \| "initialize" \| "update"` | Specifies the operation type<br>One of `'initialize'`, `'none'`, `'update'`. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `ilo` | `integer` | ILO and IHI mark the rows and columns of H which are in Hessenberg form (0-based).<br>Rejects `ilo < 1` |
| `ihi` | `integer` | ILO and IHI mark the rows and columns of H which are in Hessenberg form (0-based).<br>Rejects `ihi > N \|\| ihi < ilo - 1` |
| `H` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDH` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `H`<br>Requires `LDH ≥ N` |
| `T` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDT` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `T`<br>Requires `LDT ≥ N` |
| `ALPHAR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideALPHAR` | `integer` | Stride length for `ALPHAR` |
| `ALPHAI` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideALPHAI` | `integer` | Stride length for `ALPHAI` |
| `BETA` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideBETA` | `integer` | Stride length for `BETA` |
| `Q` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDQ` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Q` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDZ` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Z` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, N)</sub> | **out** · Output array |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `job`:

  -   `= 'E'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'S'`: Compute eigenvalues and the Schur form.
- `compq`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Left Schur vectors (Q) are not computed;
  -   `= 'I'`: Q is initialized to the unit matrix and the matrix Q of left Schur vectors of (H,T) is returned;
  -   `= 'V'`: Q must contain an orthogonal matrix Q1 on entry and the product $Q_{1} \, Q$ is returned.
- `compz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Right Schur vectors (Z) are not computed;
  -   `= 'I'`: Z is initialized to the unit matrix and the matrix Z of right Schur vectors of (H,T) is returned;
  -   `= 'V'`: Z must contain an orthogonal matrix Z1 on entry and the product $Z_{1} \, Z$ is returned.
- `N`: The order of the matrices H, T, Q, and Z. $N \ge 0$.
- `ihi`: `ILO` and `IHI` mark the rows and columns of H which are in Hessenberg form. It is assumed that A is already upper triangular in rows and columns 1:`ILO`-1 and `IHI`+1:N. If $N > 0$, $1 \le \mathrm{ILO} \le \mathrm{IHI} \le N$; if $N = 0$, `ILO=1` and `IHI=0`.
- `H`: On entry, the N-by-N upper Hessenberg matrix H. On exit, if `JOB = 'S'`, H contains the upper quasi-triangular matrix S from the generalized Schur factorization. If `JOB = 'E'`, the diagonal blocks of H match those of S, but the rest of H is unspecified.
- `T`: On entry, the N-by-N upper triangular matrix T. On exit, if `JOB = 'S'`, T contains the upper triangular matrix P from the generalized Schur factorization; 2-by-2 diagonal blocks of P corresponding to 2-by-2 blocks of S are reduced to positive diagonal form, i.e., if `H(j+1,j)` is non-zero, then $T(j+1,j) = T(j,j+1) = 0$, $T(j,j) > 0$, and $T(j+1,j+1) > 0$. If `JOB = 'E'`, the diagonal blocks of T match those of P, but the rest of T is unspecified.
- `ALPHAR`: The real parts of each scalar $\alpha$ defining an eigenvalue of GNEP.
- `ALPHAI`: The imaginary parts of each scalar $\alpha$ defining an eigenvalue of GNEP. If `ALPHAI(j)` is zero, then the j-th eigenvalue is real; if positive, then the j-th and (j+1)-st eigenvalues are a complex conjugate pair, with `ALPHAI(j+1) = -ALPHAI(j)`.
- `BETA`: The scalars $\beta$ that define the eigenvalues of GNEP. Together, the quantities $\alpha = (\mathrm{ALPHAR}(j),\mathrm{ALPHAI}(j))$ and $\beta = \mathrm{BETA}(j)$ represent the j-th eigenvalue of the matrix pair (A,B), in one of the forms $\lambda = \alpha /\beta$ or $\mu = \beta /\alpha$. Since either $\lambda$ or $\mu$ may overflow, they should not, in general, be computed.
- `Q`: On entry, if `COMPQ = 'V'`, the orthogonal matrix Q1 used in the reduction of (A,B) to generalized Hessenberg form. On exit, if `COMPQ = 'I'`, the orthogonal matrix of left Schur vectors of (H,T), and if `COMPQ = 'V'`, the orthogonal matrix of left Schur vectors of (A,B). Not referenced if `COMPQ = 'N'`.
- `Z`: On entry, if `COMPZ = 'V'`, the orthogonal matrix Z1 used in the reduction of (A,B) to generalized Hessenberg form. On exit, if `COMPZ = 'I'`, the orthogonal matrix of right Schur vectors of (H,T), and if `COMPZ = 'V'`, the orthogonal matrix of right Schur vectors of (A,B). Not referenced if `COMPZ = 'N'`.
- `WORK`: On exit, if $\mathrm{INFO} \ge 0$, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "eigenvalues", "schur"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "initialize", "none", "update"
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be one of the following: "initialize", "none", "update"
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument is invalid (rejected when `( ilo + 1 ) < 1`)
- `RangeError` seventh argument is invalid (rejected when `( ihi + 1 ) > N \|\| ( ihi + 1 ) < ( ilo + 1 ) - 1`)
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `N`
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be greater than or equal to `N`
- `RangeError` leading dimension arguments must be valid

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dhgeqz.strided(
    job, compq, compz,
    N,
    ilo, ihi,
    H, strideH1, strideH2, offsetH,
    T, strideT1, strideT2, offsetT,
    ALPHAR, strideALPHAR, offsetALPHAR,
    ALPHAI, strideALPHAI, offsetALPHAI,
    BETA, strideBETA, offsetBETA,
    Q, strideQ1, strideQ2, offsetQ,
    Z, strideZ1, strideZ2, offsetZ,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `job` | `"eigenvalues" \| "schur"` | Specifies the operation type<br>One of `'eigenvalues'`, `'schur'`. |
| `compq` | `"none" \| "initialize" \| "update"` | Specifies the operation type<br>One of `'initialize'`, `'none'`, `'update'`. |
| `compz` | `"none" \| "initialize" \| "update"` | Specifies the operation type<br>One of `'initialize'`, `'none'`, `'update'`. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `ilo` | `integer` | ILO and IHI mark the rows and columns of H which are in Hessenberg form (0-based).<br>Rejects `ilo < 1` |
| `ihi` | `integer` | ILO and IHI mark the rows and columns of H which are in Hessenberg form (0-based).<br>Rejects `ihi > N \|\| ihi < ilo - 1` |
| `H` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideH1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `H` |
| ↳ `strideH2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `H` |
| ↳ `offsetH` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `H` |

| ↳ `offsetBETA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `BETA` |
| `Q` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideQ1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `Q` |
| ↳ `strideQ2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `Q` |
| ↳ `offsetQ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `Q` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |

| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `Z` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, N)</sub> | **out** · Output array |

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N <= 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `= 1,...,N`: the QZ iteration did not converge.  (H,T) is not in Schur form, but `ALPHAR(i)`, `ALPHAI(i)`, and `BETA(i)`, $i=\mathrm{INFO}+1$,...,N should be correct. = N+1,...,$2 \, N$: the shift calculation failed.  (H,T) is not in Schur form, but `ALPHAR(i)`, `ALPHAI(i)`, and `BETA(i)`, $i=\mathrm{INFO}-N+1$,...,N should be correct.

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dhgeqz()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DHGEQZ`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dhgeqz.f).
-   The generalized eigenvalues are `(ALPHAR(j) + i*ALPHAI(j)) / BETA(j)`, for j = 0, ..., N-1.
-   `H` must be in upper Hessenberg form and `T` must be in upper triangular form on entry.
-   The function returns INFO: 0 on success, j+1 if the j-th eigenvalue failed to converge, N+1 or N+2 for unexpected failures.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dhgeqz from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dhgeqz';

// 2x2 upper Hessenberg H and upper triangular T:
const H = new Float64Array( [ 2.0, 3.0, 1.5, 4.0 ] );
const T = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 0.5, 0.0, 2.0 ] );
const ALPHAR = new Float64Array( 2 );
const ALPHAI = new Float64Array( 2 );
const BETA = new Float64Array( 2 );
const Q = new Float64Array( 4 );
const Z = new Float64Array( 4 );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 10 );

const info = dhgeqz.strided( 'eigenvalues', 'none', 'none', 2, 0, 1, H, 2, 1, 0, T, 2, 1, 0, ALPHAR, 1, 0, ALPHAI, 1, 0, BETA, 1, 0, Q, 2, 1, 0, Z, 2, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0 );

console.log( 'info:', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'ALPHAR:', ALPHAR ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'ALPHAI:', ALPHAI ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'BETA:', BETA ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DHGEQZ`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DHGEQZ computes the eigenvalues of a real matrix pair (H,T), where H is an upper Hessenberg matrix and T is upper triangular, using the double-shift QZ method. Matrix pairs of this type are produced by the reduction to generalized upper Hessenberg form of a real matrix pair (A,B):

$$
A = Q_{1} \, H \, Z_{1}^T, B = Q_{1} \, T \, Z_{1}^T
$$

as computed by DGGHRD.

If `JOB='S'`, then the Hessenberg-triangular pair (H,T) is also reduced to generalized Schur form,

$$
H = Q \, S \, Z^T, T = Q \, P \, Z^T
$$

where Q and Z are orthogonal matrices, P is an upper triangular matrix, and S is a quasi-triangular matrix with 1-by-1 and 2-by-2 diagonal blocks.

The 1-by-1 blocks correspond to real eigenvalues of the matrix pair (H,T) and the 2-by-2 blocks correspond to complex conjugate pairs of eigenvalues.

Additionally, the 2-by-2 upper triangular diagonal blocks of P corresponding to 2-by-2 blocks of S are reduced to positive diagonal form, i.e., if S(j+1,j) is non-zero, then $P(j+1,j) = P(j,j+1) = 0$, $P(j,j) > 0$, and $P(j+1,j+1) > 0$.

Optionally, the orthogonal matrix Q from the generalized Schur factorization may be postmultiplied into an input matrix Q1, and the orthogonal matrix Z may be postmultiplied into an input matrix Z1. If Q1 and Z1 are the orthogonal matrices from DGGHRD that reduced the matrix pair (A,B) to generalized upper Hessenberg form, then the output matrices $Q_{1} \, Q$ and $Z_{1} \, Z$ are the orthogonal factors from the generalized Schur factorization of (A,B):

$$
A = (Q_{1} \, Q) \, S \, (Z_{1} \, Z)^T, B = (Q_{1} \, Q) \, P \, (Z_{1} \, Z)^T
$$

To avoid overflow, eigenvalues of the matrix pair (H,T) (equivalently, of (A,B)) are computed as a pair of values ($\alpha$,$\beta$), where $\alpha$ is complex and $\beta$ real. If $\beta$ is nonzero, $\lambda = \alpha / \beta$ is an eigenvalue of the generalized nonsymmetric eigenvalue problem (GNEP)

$$
A \, x = \lambda \, B \, x
$$

and if $\alpha$ is nonzero, $\mu = \beta / \alpha$ is an eigenvalue of the alternate form of the GNEP

$$
\mu \, A \, y = B \, y
$$

Real eigenvalues can be read directly from the generalized Schur form:

$$
\alpha = S(i,i), \beta = P(i,i)
$$

Ref: C.B. Moler & G.W. Stewart, "An Algorithm for Generalized Matrix

-   Eigenvalue Problems", SIAM J. Numer. Anal., 10(1973),
-   pp. 241--256.

### Further Details

Iteration counters:

JITER -- counts iterations. IITER -- counts iterations run since ILAST was last

-   changed. This is therefore reset only when a 1-by-1 or
-   2-by-2 block deflates off the bottom.

</section>
